title: Photogalvanic transport of nonreciprocal Cooper-pair fluctuations
authors: Joaquim Telles de Miranda, Alex Levchenko
abstract: We develop a theory of the nonlinear optical and transport responses of two-dimensional noncentrosymmetric superconductors in the fluctuation regime above the transition temperature, encompassing the photogalvanic effect, second-harmonic generation, and the photovoltaic Hall effect. In the vicinity of the transition these responses are strongly enhanced by preformed Cooper pairs, whose nonreciprocity enters the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau description in two physically distinct ways: through thermodynamic Lifshitz invariants, which encode an asymmetric pair spectrum, and through kinetic Lifshitz invariants, which encode an asymmetric pair relaxation and are locked to the Langevin noise by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. We derive generalized master formulas for the paraconductivity (Aslamazov-Larkin) and the quantum-interference (Maki-Thompson) channels of the nonlinear current, valid at arbitrary drive frequency and to linear order in the nonreciprocal perturbations, and reduce them to closed-form dimensionless functions. Circular polarization discriminates sharply between the mechanisms: for reciprocal momentum-structureless noise the Aslamazov-Larkin channel is polarization insensitive and its circular photogalvanic response vanishes for any pair spectrum, whereas the Maki-Thompson channel and the nonreciprocal noise support helicity-odd rectified currents, including a fluctuation photovoltaic Hall current flowing transverse to the strain axis. Applications to Rashba-type ($C_{3v}$) and Ising-type ($D_{3h}$) superconductors demonstrate how the point-group symmetry dictates the allowed vector structures of the nonlinear currents, and how polarization analysis together with the frequency and dephasing dependences can be used to separate the individual channels experimentally.
summary: This work develops a comprehensive theory for nonlinear transport in fluctuating 2D noncentrosymmetric superconductors. It extends previous models by incorporating nonreciprocity into the kinetic relaxation terms of the Ginzburg-Landau theory. The key finding is that this kinetic nonreciprocity enables a polarization-sensitive photogalvanic response in the Aslamazov-Larkin channel, offering a clean experimental signature for nonreciprocal pair kinetics.
main_problem: Developing a theory for the nonlinear optical and transport responses (photogalvanic, SHG, photovoltaic Hall effect) in 2D noncentrosymmetric superconductors in the fluctuation regime above $T_c$.
main_result: The kinetic nonreciprocity, encoded in kinetic Lifshitz invariants, allows for a polarization-sensitive, helicity-odd rectified current in the Aslamazov-Larkin channel, which was previously only seen in the Maki-Thompson channel.
method: Derivation of generalized master formulas for the nonlinear current in the Aslamazov-Larkin and Maki-Thompson channels using the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau description.
model_or_system: Two-dimensional noncentrosymmetric superconductors operating in the fluctuation regime ($T \gtrsim T_c$). The dynamics are modeled using the stochastic TDGL equation incorporating both thermodynamic and kinetic nonreciprocal terms.
key_observables: Photogalvanic current, second-harmonic generation, photovoltaic Hall current, and their dependence on circular polarization (helicity-odd rectification).
important_parameters: Temperature relative to $T_c$, drive frequency ($\omega$), nonreciprocal perturbation strength ($\delta\alpha, ho$), and point-group symmetry ($C_{3v}, D_{3h}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed to linear order in nonreciprocal perturbations and to second order in the drive field, assuming the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem holds.
paper_structure: The paper develops the TDGL dynamics, derives generalized master formulas for the AL and MT channels (incorporating both thermodynamic and kinetic nonreciprocity), and analyzes the polarization dependence and symmetry constraints.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between non-equilibrium fluctuation dynamics (kinetic invariants) and measurable optical/transport responses (PGE, PVHE) provides a powerful tool for characterizing broken inversion symmetry in superconductors, relevant to advanced quantum materials research.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
